discovery: Proposal and realization of electron-spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (solid-state spin qubits)
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed that the spin of a single electron confined in a semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a qubit, controlled by gate voltages and exchange coupling. They also set out the criteria that any physical quantum computer must satisfy. The proposal turned the manipulation of individual spins in nanostructures into an experimental programme. Vandersypen led key realizations of it: single-shot readout of an individual electron spin, coherent single-spin control, high-fidelity two-qubit gates in silicon, and scalable, industrially manufactured spin-qubit arrays. Together these works established that single spins in solid-state devices can be coherent, controllable and measurable quantum objects. This deepened our understanding of spin coherence and decoherence in mesoscopic systems. It also opened a CMOS-compatible route toward large-scale quantum processors, complementing the superconducting circuits recognized in 2025.
